overview: This repository holds two products you can build and run. Darling is a headless collector service that keeps its data in PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB, and it comes with a WPF viewer and a web dashboard. Lite is a portable WPF app that keeps its data in DuckDB.
Both products collect data from SQL Server and answer questions through an MCP server for AI tools. They share code for collectors, alerting, notifications, analysis and plan analysis.
The Full Dashboard and the CLI installer are frozen in a zip file. Nothing in the repository builds them.

areas.name: Darling service (collectors, scheduler)
areas.description: The Darling service is the headless process that collects data. At start it reads darling.json, bootstraps the store, and then runs each collector on its schedule. Collectors that are shared with Lite live in a separate project, and the service runs them through its collector runner. The same process hosts the MCP endpoint and the web dashboard.

areas.name: Darling storage (PostgreSQL store, migrations, rollups)
areas.description: This project owns the PostgreSQL store. It holds the numbered migrations and the schema generator. It also holds the store classes that read and write each table, and the rollups and retention tiers that keep the store small. A change to a table starts with a new migration in the list. The Darling export tool also lives here, because it reads the store and writes Parquet files.

areas.name: Darling MCP
areas.description: Darling answers MCP clients from the service process. Each tool is a public static method that carries the McpServerTool attribute. The web endpoints call the same methods, so the two surfaces return the same data. A write policy decides which tools can change anything, and each change is off until an operator turns it on.

areas.name: Darling web UI and front door
areas.description: The web dashboard is plain JavaScript pages in wwwroot that call the service over HTTP. The endpoint files in the service answer those calls. The front door lets one Darling service route to other Darling services, so a team can use one address.

areas.name: Darling Viewer (WPF)
areas.description: The Viewer is a desktop app that reads from a Darling service. It shows the fleet, the server tabs, alerts and the alert rule editors. It can run on the service host or on another machine.

areas.name: Lite (WPF, DuckDB, archive and compaction)
areas.description: Lite is one WPF app that collects, stores and shows the data. A background service runs the collectors on a timer and writes to DuckDB. Older data moves to Parquet files, which a compaction step merges. A retention service deletes archive files that are past their age limit.

areas.description: Lite has its own MCP server with the same tool style as Darling. Each tool class sits in Lite/Mcp and reads from the local DuckDB data. Lite also has an investigation store that agents can read and write.
